documents: Stratovolcano: A conical volcano built up by many layers of hardened lava, tephra, pumice, and ash. Properties: steep profile, periodic explosive eruptions, andesitic to dacitic composition. Relations: subtype of volcano, associated with subduction zones

Magma Chamber: A large pool of liquid rock beneath the surface of the Earth. Properties: temperature 700-1300°C, pressure dependent depth, compositional zonation. Relations: feeds volcanic eruptions, connected to dike systems

Pyroclastic Flow: A fast-moving current of hot gas and volcanic matter. Properties: temperature 200-700°C, velocity up to 700 km/h, density stratified. Relations: produced by explosive eruptions, causes of volcanic hazards

Title: Deep learning for volcanic deformation analysis. Abstract: We present a novel deep learning approach for analyzing InSAR data to detect volcanic deformation patterns.... Keywords: InSAR, deep learning, volcanic deformation, machine learning
Volcano: Mount St. Helens. Event: Explosive eruption on 1980-05-18. Magnitude: VEI 5. Description: Lateral blast and pyroclastic flows, 57 fatalities

Material: Basalt. Composition: SiO2: 45-52%, MgO: 5-12%, CaO: 8-12%. Density: 2.8-3.0 g/cm³. Elastic properties: Young modulus: 60-100 GPa, Poisson ratio: 0.25-0.30. Thermal properties: Thermal conductivity: 1.5-2.5 W/mK, Specific heat: 840 J/kgK
